title: Host fingerprint and GPU profile spec
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note proposes a practical, incremental design for host identity ("fingerprint") and GPU capability profiles used by the service-discovery/control-plane. The objective is to enable region-aware routing policies, quick capability matching for inference requests, and robust health-driven shedding/fallback across Dedicated and Private fleet segments.

Key principles (tradeoffs called out):
- Compact identity vector: keep per-host metadata small and versioned to minimize sync cost across regions.
- Capability-first routing: match by capability vectors (memory, compute, quantization support) rather than brittle SKU strings.
- Stale-tolerant control-plane: prefer eventual consistency with strong local decision hooks to preserve SLOs when control-plane/backplane partitions occur.
- Observability and provenance: every fingerprint change is auditable; changes feed into Optimize recommendations and rollout safety checks.

Data model (compact fields for every host):
- host_id: short stable opaque id (uuid-v4)
- region: region code (e.g., us-west-2, eu-north-1)
- availability_zone: optional AZ string
- host_role: inference|batch|control|infra
- gpu_family_vector: comma-delimited family tags (e.g., a100-80gb,a100-40gb,rtx-6000)
- gpu_capabilities: semicolon-separated capability flags and numeric buckets (format: flag=val). Examples:
    - float16=1;int8=1;kv-cache=1;max-tokens=2048;free-memory-gb=40
- firmware_and_driver: driver:<version>|cuda:<version>|mlfw:<version> (used for compatibility checks)
- topology_score: small integer score representing PCIe/nvlink proximity heuristic (0-10)
- health_signature: short hash representing recent health fingerprint (see below)
- last_seen: ISO8601 timestamp
- provenance_tag: e.g., autoset, manual, provisioning-script-v2

Example line (text-friendly):
host_id=3b2f4c9a region=us-west-2 host_role=inference gpu_family_vector=a100-80gb gpu_capabilities=float16=1;int8=1;kv-cache=1;max-tokens=8192;free-memory-gb=60 firmware_and_driver=driver:525.60|cuda:12.1 topology_score=8 health_signature=hsig-20241021T1430 last_seen=2024-10-21T14:31:02Z provenance_tag=autoset

Health signature and scoring:
- Health signature is a short deterministic summary (not raw metrics) produced by an agent that samples a rolling window (e.g., 60s medians) of core signals: GPU utilization, GPU memory pressure, PCIe errors, OOM count, per-process latency anomalies, and infra heartbeat gaps.
- The agent emits a v1 health_signature: base64(sha1(host_id + snapshot-window + quantized-signal-bitmap)). This compact value is used for quick equality checks and cheap change detection by the control plane.
- A separate health_score (0-100) is stored as numeric in metrics stores, but the inventory only carries quantized buckets (healthy|degraded|unavailable) to keep inventory small.
- TTL policy: if last_seen > 90s (configurable), mark as flaky; >5m mark as stale for routing.

Sync/replication model across regions and control-plane tiers:
- Authoritative sources: each region has a local region-inventory service that is authoritative for hosts physically located in that region. A global control-plane aggregates metadata asynchronously for query/management UIs and cross-region routing decisions.
- Publish-subscribe: region-inventory publishes compact host-delta messages to a secure backplane (Kafka or NATS). Global aggregator subscribes and materializes a lightweight global view (index by host_id, region, capabilities).
- Eventual consistency: routing decisions generally query local region-inventory first; if a cross-region route is required, the router consults the global index with best-effort freshness guarantees and falls back to capacity proxies when stale.
- Snapshot vs delta: host fingerprints are snapshot-on-change; for frequent signal changes (health_signature) send deltas only when bucket moves (healthy->degraded) or on boundary-crossing.

Routing policy primitives to implement:
- capability_match(cap_vector, required_vector) -> boolean: based on numeric minima and boolean capability flags. This should be available as a library in both control-plane and in local routers.
- prefer_local_within(ms_latency_budget): boolean threshold; promotes same-region hosts when latency budgets are tight.
- fallback_chain: ordered list [same-region-high-capacity, same-region-low-capacity, cross-region-compatible, model-variant-fallback]
- canary_weighting: small percentage routing to new firmware/driver buckets for rollout validation.

Labeling vocabulary (recommended canonical keys) — choose short keys for compactness:
- r:region
- az:az
- role:role
- gvec:gpu_family_vector (comma list)
- gcap:gpu_capabilities (semi format described above)
- topo:topology_score (0-10)
- prov:provenance_tag
- hbucket:health_bucket (healthy|degraded|unavailable)

Compatibility and model-serving concerns:
- Quantization/path support: some models require int8 kernels; gcap=int8=1 must be explicitly present. Avoid inferring int8 capability from GPU model name alone.
- KV cache affinity: requests that can reuse KV-cache should prefer hosts with kv-cache=1 and topology_score>=7 (NVLink benefit).
- Mixed-precision fallbacks: if float16 missing, prefer CPU-hosted fallbacks only if the latency budget allows.

Control-plane APIs (sketch):
- GET /v1/hosts?region=us-west-2&gcap=int8=1&topo>=7 -> returns list of host_id and host_summary (compact fields).
- POST /v1/hosts/batch-update -> accept compressed delta lines (for provisioning flows).
- GET /v1/hosts/{host_id}/history -> returns audit-friendly changelog (only in global aggregator).
- SUBSCRIBE /v1/stream/region-deltas -> streaming delta feed (server-sent-events or grpc stream).

Operational notes and runbook snippets:
- Agent misbehavior: if an agent flips health_signature rapidly (churn), throttle to 1 change per 30s and mark agent for investigation.
- Driver rollouts: group hosts by firmware_and_driver fingerprint, run a staged canary by moving a small subset into canary routing group using the provenance_tag.
- Capacity emergency: allow emergency override label (prov=maintenance) that temporarily suppresses routing but preserves audit trail.

Migration path (practical steps):
1) Implement host-agent v1 producing compact fingerprint + health_signature in a canary region (us-west-2).
2) Build region-inventory with delta publish; wire the global aggregator in read-only mode for first 2 weeks to validate ingestion.
3) Add capability_match library to router service in canary, validate decisions against a shadow traffic lane for 3 days.
4) Gradually expand to more regions, enabling write-through global aggregation after cross-region fallbacks stabilized.

Open questions / tradeoffs for design review:
- Fixed bucket thresholds vs adaptive thresholds for health scoring; adaptive reduces false positives but complicates predictable routing.
- How aggressively to compact gpu_capabilities (human readability vs bandwidth).
- Whether to store full driver/firmware strings in global view or just signatures (tradeoff: debuggability vs cardinality).

Appendix: sample capability matching logic (pseudocode)
- parse request requirements -> required_gcaps map
- for each candidate host: parse host.gcap -> host_gcaps map; compare numeric minima and boolean flags; compute match_score
- prefer hosts with match_score>=1 and highest topology_score then lowest expected p99 latency estimate

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally avoids prescribing exact key names for low-level telemetry (those belong in agent spec) but recommends a compact canonical labeling set for inventory.
- Feedback requested on the trade space around health_signature TTLs and the acceptable staleness window for cross-region routing (we observed in past infra incidents that 30-90s is the key area).

Action items (owners):
- Asha: prototype agent v1 and publish sample delta stream (target: 2024-11-15).
- Marco: implement capability_match library in router (target: 2024-12-01).
- Liang: wire global aggregator read-only ingestion and dashboards (target: 2024-12-15).
- Evelyn: safety checklist for driver rollouts and provenance tagging (target: 2025-01-02).
